T0.title: harness plumbing: 3 real daemons mesh and are observable

T1.detail: regressed to gen 1 after a gen-1 echo at ttl=306 (author's own data overwritten)
T1.title: own fresh data survives a stale echo at equal TTL

T10.detail: peer never contacted: one bad line voided the whole list (CLI discover printed 0 addresses, exit=14)
T10.title: discovery survives a malformed line

T11.detail: adopted gen 3 (version=0): kept the older generation because it carried the higher TTL (280 vs 240)
T11.title: rebooted node adopts newest generation, not highest TTL

T13.detail: 40 runs completed, slowest 0.02s — not reproduced on this build (gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0); the report is against GCC 12.2/znver3
T13.title: discover never hangs (lime-packages#1198)

T14.detail: 9 syncs in 45s healthy (~9 expected), 4 with 3 blackholed peers added — publishing to a healthy peer collapsed to 44% because unrelated peers were unreachable: the publish loop connects to each discovered peer in turn with no timeout
T14.title: unreachable peers do not stop publishing to reachable ones

T15.detail: survived 10 held connections plus hook/subprocess churn at a 24-descriptor limit. Note: connections cannot starve this daemon, because the serial accept loop (T4) only ever holds ONE at a time — the rest queue in the backlog. The fatal accept path (audit B4) is therefore hard to reach today and becomes reachable the moment concurrency (T5) is fixed. Fix accept error handling in the same change.
T15.title: descriptor exhaustion does not kill the daemon

T16.detail: 400 minimal syncs, fastest round-trip 86008us — never within the sub-microsecond window that would zero the divisor (latent, not live)
T16.title: bandwidth estimation never divides by zero

T17.detail: 3/3 broken scripts (exit-3, stderr-exit-1, missing) are byte-identical to a healthy node with no neighbours: exit 0, empty output — the node stops syncing and nothing reports why
T17.title: a failing discover script is distinguishable from no peers

T18.detail: state intact and node serving after truncation at all three points (type name, length field, payload)
T18.title: truncated transfers do not corrupt state

T19.detail: file unparseable in 12/2417 reads under concurrent writers (locking is compile-time optional and OFF by default); timestamps are boot-relative (mTS=409933484174655, far below epoch nanoseconds)
T19.title: stats file survives concurrent writers

T2.detail: 4 generations reached all nodes, worst convergence 39s, no regressions
T2.title: author updates reach every node without regressions

T20.detail: stranger wrote state into the node and it is now served to the mesh: author='lime-b' (impersonating lime-b), ttl=290, data={'gen': 1, 'hostname': 'attacker', 'note': 'written by a host that is not a peer'} — no auth, and hooks consuming this run as root
T20.title: unauthenticated peers cannot inject state

T21.detail: all 8 disconnecting cases were handled, but a peer that under-delivers its declared length and stays connected stops the node serving anyone (TimeoutError) — a truncated transfer on a flaky link does exactly this, and no read has a deadline
T21.title: malformed frames rejected, node survives

T22.detail: max TTL spread **4s** across 5 nodes (tolerance 3s): {'jime': 2351, 'balcon': 2355, 'tronco': 2354, 'e-bob': 2353, 'nodo-suri': 2352}; the author held the LOWEST TTL for its own key in 4/6 samples — every neighbour's copy outranks the author's; 6 'is remote peer ill?' warning(s) — the author rejecting its own entry coming back inflated, the exact line from the MonteNet report
T22.title: TTL stays consistent across a 5-node chain (MonteNet shape)

T3.title: mesh converges after publishing stops (lossy links)

T4.detail: node stopped serving while one peer was silent (baseline 0.10s, then TimeoutError after 20s)
T4.title: a silent peer does not block the daemon

T5.detail: 12 concurrent peers took 3.5s; single session 0.39s, deadline 2.0s -> served serially (9.1x single)
T5.title: concurrent peers are not served serially

T6.detail: entry expired but no hook ran (6 invocations before and after) — downstream files keep serving the dead entry
T6.title: entry expiry notifies hooks

T7.detail: exit=2; F 1786559770.975 bool SharedState::loadRegisteredTypes(std::error_condition*)  error: 2 No such file or directory category: generic Failure opening co
T7.title: register bootstraps on a clean system

T8.detail: hook inherited: fd3 -> anon_inode:[eventpoll], fd4 -> socket:[17901980]
T8.title: hook children do not inherit daemon sockets

T9.detail: daemon exited while the config was briefly unreadable — a torn read from a concurrent `register` kills the node. Last log:   [(nil)]
T9.title: daemon survives a briefly invalid config file
